display.purpose: Store name on home (44/64/72px), card and product names on detail pages; condensed 87.5%.

headline.purpose: Section titles under the 2px ink rule (30px phone, 36px desktop).

title.purpose: Row names, set names, list titles.

number.purpose: Collector numbers, prices, counts, market readings; condensed tabular cut, 12-34px.

stamp.purpose: Set codes, grader names, grade labels, pre-order stamp, box-end codes; 75% width, uppercase. Labels data, never headings.

label.purpose: Column heads and field labels in paper-ink-3, sentence case.

shadows.name: slab-case

shadows.purpose: The clear case of a graded slab.

shadows.name: box-end
shadows.purpose: The sealed product face and its foot band.

shadows.name: line-stroke
shadows.purpose: Outlined secondary button; a stroke, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: The one easing for every transition in the shell and slice.

motion.name: row-print
motion.value: 520ms, 28ms stagger per row; translateY(6px) and opacity
motion.purpose: Rows print in by number, once.

motion.name: card-peek
motion.purpose: The card slides out of its number slot (pointer, 768px and up); opacity only under reduced motion.

themeBridge.note: The card slice (features/storefront/components/cards) reads only --tc-* tokens. Inside .cx-sf they map to the checklist stock (--color-cx-*), with the accent following the store hue. Outside it (platform pages under features/platform/card-shop) they map to the dashboard theme: --background, --muted, --foreground, --muted-foreground, --border, and a fixed accent oklch(84% 0.165 92). DESIGN.md governs the storefront mapping.

narrative.overview:
Every set is a numbered sheet printed on black checklist stock. Rows are paper-white type on hairline rules; each one carries a tick box, the collector number, the card's name, its rarity mark, a condition run, the dated market reading, the shop's price and an Add. A card opens from its number: on a pointer the art slides out of the number slot beside the row, on touch tapping the number opens it in place. Lists everywhere (home shelves, set pages, the buylist, the binder) are the same sheet read for a different purpose; the buylist is the sheet read as what the shop is buying.

The page is dense the way a printed checklist is dense: one fixed column grid, tabular numbers, no card-grid chrome. Colour is withheld so the set logos and card art carry it; the only ink accent is card-border yellow, the store's own logo hue, set per store. Depth is nearly absent: the sheet is flat, a hovered row lifts one step in tone, and the only objects that read as physical are the things being sold (the card with its rounded corners, the graded slab, the sealed box end).

The world rejects the marketplace grid of identical product cards and the holographic-gradient glow page.
keyCharacteristics: Black stock, paper-white rows, hairline rules; a 2px ink rule opens every sheet and every section.
One control shape: the square tick box, with a state ramp (solid in stock, hollow out, dashed wanted or pre-order).
One accent, card-border yellow, hue-driven from the store's logo colour.
Archivo throughout: condensed cut for numbers, codes and stamps, normal width for names and reading.
Square corners on everything the shop prints; rounded corners only on depicted objects (cards, slabs).
Motion is printing: rows print in by number once, a tick inks in, the card slides out of its slot.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Card-border yellow is the only accent. It marks what the shop holds and what the collector can do next; it never fills a background band, a heading, or a decorative field. A chosen option that is not a buy action (a "have" or a filter in a form) is selected in paper ink, not yellow.

rules.name: The Store Hue Rule
rules.body: The accent's hue comes from the store's logo colour on the shell wrapper; never hard-code a yellow hex in storefront code.

rules.name: The Art Carries Colour Rule
rules.body: Set logos and card art are the page's colour. Gold rarity stars use the accent because the card prints them gold; nothing else borrows it for ornament.

rules.name: The Condensed Number Rule
rules.body: Every number a collector compares (No., price, market, count, grade) sets in the condensed tabular cut; names never do.

rules.name: The Stamp Is Data Rule
rules.body: Uppercase stamps label a datum (a code, a grade, a state). They never sit above a heading as a section label.

rules.name: The One Grid Rule
rules.body: Every list of cards uses the sheet's column grid (No., Name, Rarity, Run, Market, Price); a changed price restyles its cell without breaking the grid.

rules.name: The Kept Place Rule
rules.body: A sold-out card keeps its row and number, its name struck through, offering the want list; the sheet never closes up.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing printed on the sheet casts a shadow and nothing glows. Elevation belongs to objects being sold and to overlays that float above the page.

rules.name: The Square Tick Rule
rules.body: The tick box is the one control shape. Its state ramp is the vocabulary for stock and intent: solid yellow with an inked check for in stock or owned, hollow paper-ink-3 for out, dashed yellow for wanted or pre-order, hairline for not stocked.

dos: Do put every list of cards on the sheet grid, with the number first and the price right-aligned in the condensed tabular cut.
Do keep sold-out rows in place, struck through, with Want as the action.
Do show every market reading with its date beneath it.
Do derive the accent from the store's logo hue (`hsl(var(--cx-h) 92% 60%)`), and use it only for held stock, the next action, selection and focus.
Do open sections with a 2px paper-ink rule and a headline, with the section's link underlined in yellow.
Do mark pre-orders with the dashed stamp and dashed tick.
Do read the slice's `--tc-*` tokens in card UI; the storefront shell (`.cx-sf`) maps them to the checklist stock, and platform pages map them to the dashboard theme.
donts: Don't build a marketplace grid of identical product cards for singles; grids are for objects (slabs, sealed product, art).
Don't use holographic, foil or glow gradients, or any colour gradient, on the page.
Don't fill bands, headings or pre-order fields with yellow.
Don't give printed elements (rows, ticks, run cells, inputs) rounded corners or shadows.
Don't set names in the condensed cut or numbers at normal width.
Don't place uppercase stamps above headings as section labels.
Don't introduce a second display or serif face; Archivo is the only family.
